editorial:
Imagine waking up to find your son has been snatched by a creepy guy who wants to turn kids with superpowers into living weapons. That is exactly what happens to Peter, a CIA agent who just wants his boy back. You will quickly find yourself rooting for him as he teams up with Gillian, a girl who can move things with her mind. The whole movie feels like a wild ride from the start, mixing spy movie action with scary psychic powers. It has a strange, moody energy that makes you feel like something bad is always about to happen around the corner.

What really hits home is how the movie handles the psychic fights. They are surprising and keep you on the edge of your seat. While some of the 1970s acting feels a bit over the top, it actually adds to the charm of the film. If you like stories about mind control and secret government plots, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a huge psychic battle between Peter and the villain, Childress. Just when it looks like Childress has won, Gillian uses her telekinesis to blast him. The blast is so strong that it basically knocks him apart. After the fight, Peter finally reunites with his son, Robin. They leave the madness behind and head home, knowing the dangerous psychic experiments have finally come to an end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school psychic thrillers and 70s cinema.
